gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the mic route costs compared with a headset. Maono's PD200XS mic-and-boom-arm set is $89.99, which is 1.92 times the $46.99 EKSA E900 Pro headset, and the set still has no headphones. Its XLR sensitivity is −52 dBV against −42 dBV for the HyperX Cloud III boom mic, a 10 dB gap, so it gives about 3.2 times less signal per pascal and needs gain or close placement.
standout_why: ChatGPT's search returned no results and cited no pages. Its answer is a qualitative table that says a mic 'can cost more' and a headset is 'often cheaper overall', with no prices, no ratios and no sensitivity figures. That means there is no rival page to compare against, and the answer it gave the shopper has no numbers at all. Our current page lists PD200XS, E900 Pro and DGM20 prices dated 2026-11-06 but does not compare them, does not price the boom arm separately, and has no mic sensitivity figures.
decides: This confirms the headset is the default pick for gaming and Discord. A full voice-and-audio setup costs $46.99 with the E900 Pro. The cheapest desk mic, the Maono DGM20 at $43.99, is only $3 cheaper than that headset but plays no audio. The dynamic-mic route, the PD200XS at $89.99 or the ModMic USB at $89.95, roughly doubles the spend before the shopper buys any headphones. Pick the mic route only if they already own good headphones or want to stream. In that case the PD200XS set is the best value: buying the PD200X mic ($80.99) and a BA37 arm ($54.99) separately costs $45.99 more.
